chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Dawud ibn Farqad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Every beast with fangs and every bird with talons is forbidden."
ai.seo_question: Which animals are considered haram to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *al-kulhu dhū nāb* (all fanged beasts) and *al-kulhu dhū miḫlab* (all taloned birds) as haram, reflecting the Shia juristic view that predatory animals are inherently impure or unfit for consumption. It serves as a foundational text for distinguishing between herbivorous/carnivorous animals in *fiqh*, emphasizing the physical characteristics of the animal as the primary criterion for permissibility.
